description: Linux CI drill proving the parser supervisor terminates and reaps more than the direct worker: a test worker starts one child in the same process group, both are independently discovered through /proc before cancellation, context cancellation returns promptly, and every captured /proc process entry disappears after Parse returns. This remains synthetic local CI evidence and is not host/container restart or reviewed production-artifact evidence.
requiredAssertions: worker emits a complete frame before cancellation
at least two marked processes are visible in /proc before cancellation
the child inherits the supervised worker process group
cancellation returns context.Canceled within one second
Parse returns only after the direct worker wait path has run
every captured worker or child /proc entry disappears within three seconds after Parse returns
raw process identifiers are not persisted in evidence
implementationGuards: supervisor starts workers with Setpgid true
supervisor cancellation kills negative worker pid with SIGKILL
test child is started without a new process group and therefore inherits the worker group
test captures process identifiers only in memory and emits aggregate counts only
limitations: one synthetic child process is created by the test worker
the drill verifies process-group termination and /proc disappearance but not a host or container restart
the test harness binary is not a reviewed production parser artifact
production-equivalent environment generation is not required or claimed
